mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >50% of FEDFUNDS > 4.0 regimes, or IC > 0.05 over 5-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate corporate profit expansion.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous 3 months AND UNRATE < previous 3 months
failure_condition: IC < -0.1 over 2-year rolling windows during labor strengthening phases, or 60-day returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in consumer spending proxies (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates shifting demand composition toward services, which predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates sustained economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND INDPRO < previous month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in >40% of identified demand shifts, or IC < 0.05 over 6-month windows.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below trend suggests supply-side softness, which precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates profit compression.
failure_condition: IC > 0.08 over 1-year periods during contraction phases, or 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% suggests accelerating inflation, which drives the Federal Reserve to raise rates, resulting in a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >70% of CPIAUCSL > 2.0 events, or IC < -0.2 over 6-month windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% for three months indicates a robust labor market, which supports a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return via higher wage growth expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in >50% of tightness regimes, or IC > 0.1 over 1-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, it signals aggressive tightening, which predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate reduced credit and equity valuations.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are non-negative in >60% of such events, or IC > 0.15 over 1-month windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 (trend) for two months suggests supply chain expansion, which typically precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates production capacity utilization.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1) in >50% of expansion phases, or IC < -0.05 over 4-month windows.
